appraisal_events.evidence: Je te dirai... qu’il a cru devoir lancer contre Brichot quelques insinuations venimeuses et assez ridicules... c’était une manière de nous atteindre, de bêcher notre dîner. — c’est le raté, le petit individu envieux de tout ce qui est un peu grand. En réalité il n’y avait pas un fidèle qui ne fût plus malveillant que Swann; mais tous ils avaient la précaution d’assaisonner leurs médisances... tandis que la moindre réserve que se permettait Swann... paraissait une perfidie.
appraisal_events.explanation: The Verdurins publicly condemn Swann as envious and spiteful for supposed remarks against Brichot, even though the narrator explicitly notes this judgment is unfair — every one of the 'faithful' was in fact more malicious, but only Swann's reserve is read as treachery.

status_effects.explanation: The Verdurins openly brand Swann envious and small next to Brichot, deepening the household's turn against him despite the narrator's note that this is unjust.
The passage explicitly states that Swann is threatened with 'disgrâce' among the Verdurins — his standing in the little clan is visibly eroding even though he remains unaware of it.
